# @passport

> Handle (user ID) manager and input assist for the AT Protocol (atproto) ecosystem.

## Summary

@passport allows users to manage multiple atproto handles and securely assist with handle input across relying party (RP) applications.
In modern Chromium browsers (141+), @passport serves as a W3C Federated Credential Management (FedCM) Identity Provider (IdP) for browser-native handle selection without DOM injection or invasive permissions. For unsupported browsers and environments, it provides seamless Web redirect callbacks and browser extension tools.

> **Security Boundary**: Information returned by @passport (`username`, `did`, and `token`) represents handle-selection and input hints rather than authentication credentials. The `token` is not a bearer token or access token. Relying parties must complete standard atproto OAuth using the selected `username` to authenticate the user and establish sessions.

## Core Features

- **FedCM Handle Input Assist**: Browser-native account selection UI (`IdentityCredential`) in Chrome/Chromium 141+ via `requestHandleAssist()`.
- **Web Redirect & Callback**: HTTP redirect flow (`/authentication`, `/add`) returning `username` (standard), `handle` (backward-compatible alias), `did`, `pdsurl`, and CSRF `atpstate`.
- **Client SDK (`@atpassport/client`)**: TypeScript library supporting FedCM assist (`requestHandleAssist`), callback parsing (`parseCallback`), and pre-built UI components.
- **Handle Management**: Register, reorder, and manage multiple atproto handles linked to a signed, secure session (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`).
- **Device Sync**: Transfer handles across devices using secure QR codes.
- **Developer Portal**: Domain verification for FedCM client IDs and registration of privacy policy and terms of service URLs.
- **Browser Extension**: Fallback assistant and toolbar manager for Chrome and Firefox.

## Quick Integration

### 1. FedCM Handle Assist (`@atpassport/client`)

```typescript
import { requestHandleAssist } from '@atpassport/client/core';

// Request native account chooser
const result = await requestHandleAssist({
  targetInput: document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input[name="handle"]') ?? undefined,
});

if (result) {
  // Use the input hint to initiate atproto OAuth
  await startAtprotoOAuth(result.username);
}
```

### 2. Web Redirect Callback (`parseCallback`)

When redirecting to @passport (`/authentication?callback=...&atpstate=...`), the user is redirected back with query parameters: `username`, `handle`, `did`, `pdsurl`, `atpstate`.

```typescript
import { AtPassport } from '@atpassport/client/core';

const passport = new AtPassport({
  callbackUrl: 'https://your-app.com/callback',
});

const result = passport.parseCallback(window.location.href, expectedState);
// result.username - Authenticated handle / username (e.g., 'alice.bsky.social')
// result.handle   - Alias of username for backward compatibility
// result.did      - Account DID
// result.pdsUrl   - User PDS URL
// result.customParams - Any pass-through custom query parameters
```

- [About](https://atpassport.net/en/about) - Detailed information and FAQ.
- [Developer Guide (EN)](https://atpassport.net/en/developers/guide) - Integration guide for relying parties.
- [Developer Guide (JA)](https://atpassport.net/ja/developers/guide) - 日本語開発者向け導入ガイド.
- [Developer Portal](https://atpassport.net/en/developers) - Domain verification and FedCM settings.

- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/usounds/atpassport) - Source code and client libraries.
- [NPM (@atpassport/client)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@atpassport/client) - Client library for developers.
